public_rationale: The evidence points both ways, and the answer depends on what 'pure scaling' and 'diminishing returns' mean. Reuters reported in November 2024 that Ilya Sutskever said results from scaling up pretraining had plateaued. That supports the claim for pretraining. But METR found that the length of tasks AI agents can finish kept doubling about every seven months, possibly faster in 2024. Those gains mix scaling with new methods, so they neither confirm nor refute 'pure scaling'. The AGI clause looks forward and AGI is undefined. No source isolates returns to pure scaling, so I cannot settle the claim.
limitations: The Reuters text was read through a reprint, because the original was blocked.
The key report Marcus cites could not be read.
